question: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts would you use to go to the previously opened program?
solution:
The correct answer is Alt + Shift + Tab [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****1. Alt + Shift + Tab (Option 1):**

This shortcut cycles through open programs or windows in the reverse order.

If you press Alt + Shift + Tab once, it will switch to the previously opened program (the one you were using before the current program).

This is the most accurate shortcut for going to the previously opened program.

**2. Alt + Tab (Option 2):**

This shortcut cycles through open programs or windows in the forward order.

If you press Alt + Tab once, it will switch to the most recently used program.

While this is a common shortcut for switching between programs, it does not specifically target the previously opened program.

**3. Ctrl + N (Option 3):**

This shortcut is used to open a new window or document in many applications (e.g., a new browser tab or a new file in a text editor).

It has no connection to switching between programs.

**4. Ctrl + Home (Option 4):**

This shortcut is used to move the cursor to the beginning of a document or page.

It is unrelated to switching between programs.
